clue.text: Technique following IVF? Spot female's inside

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so one piece sits in the middle of the other

blocks.note: a zit is a pimple
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A fertility clinic asks what comes after IVF, and someone notices a woman's spot.
explanation.walkthrough: ZIFT is zygote intrafallopian transfer, a fertility procedure developed as a variant on IVF; the question mark marks the definition as loose.
explanation.definitionFit: ZIFT is an assisted-conception method in which a fertilised egg is placed in the fallopian tube, a refinement of in vitro fertilisation.

clue.text: Sleuth going after vitality, old, of early Mexican

indicators.note: going after says one piece follows the others in the down light

blocks.note: zap is energy, pep
O is the abbreviation for old
tec is short for detective

explanation.surface: A detective follows an energetic old trail into early Mexican history.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival: 'of early Mexican' means relating to an early Mexican people, which the adjective use of the answer gives.
explanation.definitionFit: The Zapotec are an indigenous people of Oaxaca whose civilisation predates the Aztecs, and the name serves as an adjective too.

clue.text: Commander's staff following former walk behind battlements up

indicators.note: in a down light, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: f. is the abbreviation for following
alure is an obsolete word for a walkway along the battlements of a castle

explanation.surface: A commander carries his staff on a walk behind the battlements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former' flags the old word alure, a parapet walk, which goes up after F.
explanation.definitionFit: A ferula is a rod or staff, in particular a staff of office or authority such as a commander or prelate might carry.

clue.text: Offspring once raised, I vacated territory

indicators.note: raised in a down light means turned to read upwards, bottom to top
vacated means left empty, so that letter moves out of the word

blocks.note: fruit is an old word for offspring, as in fruit of the womb
taken as written: the letter to remove

explanation.surface: A parent recalls raising offspring and then leaving the family patch.
explanation.walkthrough: FRUIT read upwards gives TIURF; take out the I and TURF remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Turf is informal for one's own patch or area of control, as in a gang defending its turf.

clue.text: Wretched rotter O. C. interrupting crown? That was it!

definitions.text: Wretched rotter O. C. interrupting crown? That was it!

indicators.note: wretched means in a sorry, broken state, so these letters are knocked into a new order
to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged; O.C. are Oliver Cromwell's initials
the pate is the crown of the head

explanation.surface: A royalist sneers at Cromwell, the wretched rotter who broke into the reign of the Crown.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: Oliver Cromwell's rule broke the line of the Crown between Charles I and Charles II.
explanation.definitionFit: The Protectorate was the period 1653 to 1659 when England was ruled by a Lord Protector instead of a monarch.

clue.text: Chewy sweets showing that special magic, almost tops

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: juju is West African magic, or the special power of a charm
tops as an adjective means the best

explanation.surface: A confectioner's chewy sweets show a special magic that is nearly the best.
explanation.definitionFit: Jujubes are gummy fruit-flavoured lozenges, originally flavoured with the jujube berry.

clue.text: Whizzing in jet has reduced yen for cheap bus

indicators.note: whizzing about means spinning wildly, so these letters are thrown into a new order
reduced means cut right down, here to a single opening letter

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
the first letter of yen

explanation.surface: Someone flying in a jet longs less for a cheap bus ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A jitney is an American term for a small bus or shared car carrying passengers for a low fare.

clue.text: Risking damage to Jag I rode, spin out of control

indicators.note: something out of control careers about at random, so these letters lose their order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A driver nearly wrecks the Jaguar they were riding in when it spins out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damage' looks like the anagram signal but belongs to the definition; the signal is at the far end.
explanation.definitionFit: To jeopardise something is to put it in danger, so jeopardising it is exposing it to the chance of harm.

clue.text: Capital hoax, a stunner

blocks.note: bam is an old word for a hoax or trick
taken as written
a KO, knockout, is a blow that stuns

explanation.surface: A first-rate hoax, a real stunner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' reads as an adjective meaning excellent, but it is the noun: a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bamako is the capital city of Mali, on the Niger river in West Africa.

clue.text: Timeless depravity? Bird one found trapped by that

indicators.note: trapped by means caught and held inside, so these pieces sit within the other

blocks.note: evil is wickedness, depravity
a tern is a seabird
a means one

explanation.surface: A moralist calls depravity eternal, and a bird is caught up in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' points back to the depravity word, which holds the bird and one.
explanation.definitionFit: Eviternal is a rare word meaning everlasting, without end in time.

clue.text: Gob (in local parlance) ready to swallow a piece of pizza …

indicators.note: a single piece here is one letter, the one at the start
swallowing takes something inside, so the outer word holds the other

blocks.note: set means ready, as in ready, steady, go
the first letter of pizza

explanation.surface: A hungry local, ready to gobble a slice of pizza.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gob' is a verb here, to spit, not the mouth; 'in local parlance' marks a dialect form.
explanation.definitionFit: Spet is a Scots and dialect form of spit, and to gob is slang for to spit.

clue.text: Oil-yielding plants pounded in ritual, see

indicators.note: pounded means beaten to bits, so these letters are crushed into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Oily plants are crushed as part of a ritual, look.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleurites is the genus of trees including the candlenut and tung, whose seeds yield oil.

clue.text: … Herein? It's dry with upturned artificial topping

indicators.note: upturned in a down light means the word is read from the bottom up
topping says this piece goes on top, first in the down light

blocks.note: art. is the abbreviation for artificial
TT means teetotal, so dry

explanation.surface: Continuing the pizza clue: a dry pizza with fake topping turned over.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 9 down: 'Herein' is where that pizza is eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Tratt is an informal shortening of trattoria, an Italian restaurant where pizza is served.

clue.text: Standard nonsense from one of the polls?

blocks.note: par is the standard or norm
rot is nonsense

explanation.surface: An opinion poll's usual nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'polls' looks like opinion polls, but a Poll or Polly is the stock name for a parrot.
explanation.definitionFit: Poll is a traditional pet name for a parrot, so one of the polls is a parrot.

clue.text: Dashing Romeo, one taken in as fellow lodger

indicators.note: dashing means rushing about, so these letters are scattered into a new order
taken in means admitted inside, so that piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A dashing Romeo is taken in as a fellow lodger.
explanation.definitionFit: Roomie is informal for roommate, someone sharing your lodgings.

clue.text: Salad veg chic cooks featured in broadcast?

indicators.note: to cook is to alter, so these letters are worked into a new order
featured in means appearing inside, so that piece sits within the other

blocks.note: radio is a broadcast medium
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A stylish chef cooks salad on a broadcast cookery show.
explanation.definitionFit: Radicchio is a red-leaved Italian chicory used in salads.

clue.text: Sheet of wadding required by combat troops

indicators.note: required by here means held within the following words, which carry the answer across their join

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Combat troops need sheets of padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A batt is a sheet of cotton or wool wadding used in quilting or insulation.

clue.text: Story about keel Kate steered, in pidgin?

indicators.note: steered means turned this way and that, so these letters are redirected into a new order
about means around, so the outer word wraps the rest

blocks.note: a tale is a story
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A yarn about a boat Kate steered, told in pidgin.
explanation.definitionFit: Talkee-talkee is a dated term for a broken or pidgin English, a jargon used for trade.

clue.text: Entry for Cambridge housed in mixed yard — Fitzwilliam?

indicators.note: the entry to a word is its opening letter
housed in means lodged inside, so that letter goes within the other letters
mixed means jumbled, so these letters take a new order

blocks.note: the first letter of Cambridge
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An application to Cambridge, perhaps to Fitzwilliam College, sits in a jumbled yard.
explanation.walkthrough: Fitzwilliam is a Cambridge college, which the surface leans on; here it is a first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitzwilliam Darcy is the hero of Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice, usually called Mr Darcy.

clue.text: Peers deciding cases involving their fellows rule in groups of three

definitions.text: Peers deciding cases involving their fellows

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: trios are groups of three
R is the abbreviation for rule

explanation.surface: Peers sit in threes to rule on cases about their fellow peers.
explanation.definitionFit: Triors were the peers who tried a fellow peer indicted for treason or felony, in the old House of Lords procedure.

clue.text: Cricket club in tailored suede turn out well

indicators.note: tailored means cut and refashioned, so these letters are remade in a new order
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
CC is the abbreviation for cricket club

explanation.surface: Cricket club members in tailored suede look smart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn out well' suggests being well dressed, but it means to have a good result.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed is to achieve the desired outcome, which is what an undertaking does when it turns out well.

clue.text: Poisonous plant I stayed away from, in case? More than one of them

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: I + cut: to cut a class is to stay away from it

blocks.clueFragment: case? More than one of them
blocks.note: ca. is an abbreviation for cases, more than one case

explanation.surface: Someone avoided a poisonous plant just in case, as there were several.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More than one of them' turns 'case' into its plural, whose abbreviation holds the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Cicuta is the water hemlock genus, among the most poisonous plants in North America.

clue.text: Unplaced twice? Syce troubled about that calls for attention

indicators.note: troubled means stirred up, so these letters are disturbed into a new order
about means around, so these letters wrap the other piece

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged; a syce is a groom in India
0 marks an unplaced finish in racing form, so two of them

explanation.surface: A groom, upset that his horse was unplaced twice, shouts for attention.
explanation.walkthrough: In a racehorse's form figures a 0 means it finished unplaced, read here as the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooey, or cooee, is the Australian bush call used to attract someone's attention at a distance.

clue.text: A post-prandial tipple showing the way it should go

definitions.text: showing the way it should go

blocks.note: taken as written
port is a fortified wine drunk after dinner

explanation.surface: An after-dinner glass of port shows which way it should be passed.
explanation.walkthrough: By custom the port decanter goes round the table to the left, so the drink itself points to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Aport is a nautical adverb meaning to or towards the port, or left, side of a ship.

clue.text: The old spurn successive characters in trendies' day nursery

indicators.note: successive characters in means a run of letters taken straight from the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned folk scorn a trendy parents' day nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old' marks an archaic word; SDAYN is Spenser's spelling of disdain.
explanation.definitionFit: Sdayn is an obsolete Spenserian form of disdain, to scorn or reject.

clue.text: Rations go quickly on board ship

indicators.note: on board means inside a vessel, so that piece goes within the other

blocks.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
to hare is to run fast

explanation.surface: Supplies run out fast aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rations' is a noun on the surface but the answer works as either noun or verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Shares are allotted portions, just as rations are fixed allowances given to each person.

clue.text: Radical squeal over confused state

indicators.note: in a down light, over means placed above the next piece

blocks.note: a yip is a short high cry
pie, or pi, is a jumbled mess, from printers' spilt type

explanation.surface: A radical squeals about the muddled state of the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yippie was a member of the 1960s US Youth International Party, a radical counter-culture group.

clue.text: Caliph is excited about peeler with nothing on? Such'll turn one on

indicators.note: with joins the two short pieces side by side
excited means stirred up, so these letters are agitated into a new order
about means around, so these letters wrap the other piece

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
a peeler is an old slang word for a policeman, after Robert Peel
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A caliph gets excited over a naked stripper, a sight to turn anyone on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peeler' suggests a stripper, but in crosswords it is a policeman; 'Such' points back to the naked peeler as the thing that arouses.
explanation.definitionFit: A scopophiliac takes sexual pleasure in looking, so a naked body is the kind of sight that arouses such a person.

clue.text: US yacht is daunting, stem to bow

indicators.note: moving the stern letter round to the bow takes the last letter and puts it at the front

blocks.note: cows means intimidates, daunts

explanation.surface: An American yacht looks intimidating from end to end.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue read 'stern to bow': the final letter sails round to the front. 'Stem' here is a transcription slip, since a stem is already the bow.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US a scow is a flat-bottomed sailing yacht raced on inland lakes, as well as a barge.

clue.text: Junk clubs in bag

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: to bag is to bulge or sag
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: Rubbish golf clubs are stuffed in a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junk' looks like rubbish, but it is slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: Junk and scag are both slang terms for heroin.

clue.text: Wales to Scotland, post redirected

indicators.note: redirected means sent a different way, so these letters are put in another order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Mail from Wales is forwarded to Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wales' is not the country: to wale is a Scots verb meaning to choose, so 'Wales to Scotland' means what a Scot would mean by wales.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, wale means to choose or pick out, so the Scottish wales means chooses.

clue.text: Timid person boarding e.g. Berlin plane

indicators.note: boarding means getting on and inside a vehicle, so that piece goes within the other

explanation.definitionFit: The chenar is the oriental plane tree, common in Kashmir and Iran.

clue.text: Place to tuck into excellent ice cream?

explanation.walkthrough: 'tuck into' suggests eating, but it signals one piece going inside another; the question mark covers the ice cream being one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Raspberry ripple is a popular ice cream with streaks of sauce, often just called ripple.

clue.text: Unlikely to miss wine in vat, i.e. blended

indicators.note: blended means mixed together, so these letters take a new order

tent is a deep red Spanish wine

clue.text: Doctor taking in obese golfer? There are four of them

indicators.note: taking in means admitting inside, so the first piece holds the second

explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic hint with no synonym in it: the answer is a set of exactly four.

clue.text: Consult date for issue

blocks.note: to see a doctor is to consult one
